stem: A contract commits a provider to 99.95% monthly availability with service credits if it is missed. Which agreement is this?

options.text: An SLA
options.why: Measurable service levels with consequences for missing them is exactly what a service level agreement defines.

options.text: An MOU
options.why: An MOU records mutual intent and is usually not binding. It would not carry service credits.

options.text: An MSA
options.why: The master service agreement sets the umbrella terms of the relationship. The measurable targets sit in the SLA underneath it.

options.text: A BPA
options.why: A business partners agreement governs a joint venture between two businesses, including how profits are shared.

stem: An organisation signs one document covering payment terms, liability and confidentiality for all future work with a consultancy, then issues separate documents for each individual project. What are these two documents?

options.text: A master service agreement, then statements of work under it
options.why: The MSA is negotiated once as the umbrella. Each engagement is then defined by its own SOW covering deliverables, timeline and price.

options.text: A memorandum of agreement, then service level agreements
options.why: An MOA sets out roles and responsibilities between parties. SLAs define measurable service levels, not project deliverables.

options.text: A business partners agreement, then work orders
options.why: A BPA is for a joint business venture, which is not what buying consultancy is.

options.text: A non-disclosure agreement, then statements of work
options.why: An NDA only covers confidentiality. It could not carry payment terms and liability.

stem: Two public sector bodies document their shared intention to cooperate on a data sharing initiative. The document explicitly states it creates no legal obligations. What is it?

options.text: An MOU
options.why: A memorandum of understanding records mutual intent and is normally non-binding, which the document says explicitly.

options.text: An MOA
options.why: An MOA goes further, assigning defined roles and responsibilities, and is normally binding.

options.text: An SLA
options.why: An SLA sets measurable performance commitments, which a non-binding statement of intent cannot.

options.text: An MSA
options.why: A master service agreement is a binding commercial umbrella contract.

stem: Legal wants the ability to inspect a critical supplier's security controls directly, at a time of the company's own choosing, for the life of the contract. What must be negotiated?

options.text: A right-to-audit clause
options.why: Only a contractual right to audit gives you inspection on your schedule and your scope. It has to be agreed before signing.

options.text: A requirement for an annual SOC 2 report
options.why: Strong independent assurance, and its scope and timing are chosen by the vendor, not by you.

options.text: An annual security questionnaire
options.why: A questionnaire is the vendor's own account of its controls. It is the weakest form of assurance available.

options.text: A non-disclosure agreement covering the assessment
options.why: An NDA protects information exchanged. It grants no inspection right at all.

stem: A company's critical SaaS vendor depends on a single small provider for authentication. Which activity is designed to reveal this kind of exposure?

options.text: Supply chain analysis
options.why: It looks past the direct vendor to the vendor's own suppliers, which is where fourth-party risk hides.

options.text: A right-to-audit clause
options.why: That gives you the right to inspect your vendor. It does not automatically extend down to their suppliers.

options.text: A penetration test of the vendor
options.why: A test probes the vendor's exposed systems. It does not map their commercial dependencies.

options.text: A service level agreement with stronger penalties
options.why: Penalties compensate you after an outage. They do not reveal or reduce the dependency.

stem: Two companies sign a document committing to four hour response on critical incidents, with service credits if it is missed. A separate document, signed first, sets the payment terms and liability covering all work between them. Name them in order.

options.text: SLA, and the MSA signed first
options.why: The SLA carries the measurable commitment and its penalty. The MSA is the umbrella agreed once, covering everything underneath it.

options.text: MOU, and the SOW signed first
options.why: An MOU records intent and normally binds nobody, so it could not carry service credits. A SOW defines one piece of work, not the umbrella terms.

options.text: BPA, and the NDA signed first
options.why: A BPA governs a joint business venture. An NDA covers confidentiality only and carries no payment terms.

options.text: SOW, and the SLA signed first
options.why: Reversed and mislabelled. The measurable uptime promise is the SLA, not the SOW.

stem: A vendor passed due diligence two years ago and has not been reviewed since. Which practice addresses this gap?

options.text: Ongoing vendor monitoring with periodic reassessment
options.why: A vendor's security posture changes after signing. Monitoring through the life of the contract is the ongoing duty, and it is due care rather than due diligence.

options.text: A more detailed questionnaire at onboarding
options.why: That strengthens the one-time check at the start. It does nothing about the two years since.

options.text: A non-disclosure agreement covering the review
options.why: An NDA governs confidentiality of information exchanged. It triggers no review.

options.text: Accepting the risk and recording it in the register
options.why: Acceptance is a legitimate treatment and is not an answer to 'we stopped looking'.

stem: Your critical SaaS vendor subcontracts its storage to a provider you have no contract with. What is this exposure called, and which activity surfaces it?

options.text: Fourth-party risk, surfaced by supply chain analysis
options.why: Your vendor's vendors are a dependency you inherit without a contractual relationship. Supply chain analysis is what maps them.

options.text: Insider threat, surfaced by user behaviour analytics
options.why: Nobody inside either organisation is acting improperly. This is a structural dependency.

options.text: Shadow IT, surfaced by asset discovery
options.why: Shadow IT is technology your own staff adopted outside the approved process. The vendor's subcontractor is not that.

options.text: Third-party risk, surfaced by a right-to-audit clause
options.why: A right-to-audit clause reaches your direct vendor. It does not automatically extend down to their suppliers, which is exactly the gap.

stem: A supplier was assessed thoroughly during onboarding four years ago. It has since been acquired, moved its hosting offshore and lost two senior security staff. Nothing was reassessed. Which process failed?

options.text: Vendor monitoring: the ongoing activity that notices the relationship has changed since it was assessed
options.why: Due diligence answered whether to engage them, and it answered it about a company that no longer exists in that form. Monitoring is what keeps the picture current.

options.text: Due diligence, which should have anticipated the acquisition
options.why: Due diligence assesses the supplier as it is. It cannot foresee an acquisition four years out, which is exactly why monitoring exists alongside it.

options.text: The right-to-audit clause was never exercised
options.why: A useful mechanism, and the gap is that nothing prompted anyone to use it. Monitoring is what generates that prompt.

options.text: The service level agreement was not renegotiated
options.why: An SLA defines performance commitments. It is not the mechanism for tracking a vendor's risk posture.

stem: A vendor supplies a security assessment of itself, performed by a consultancy that is also the vendor's reseller and earns commission on its sales. What is the correct response?

options.text: Treat the assessment as compromised by a conflict of interest and seek genuinely independent assurance
options.why: Independence is a precondition for the finding to mean anything. An assessor with a commercial stake in the outcome cannot provide it, whatever the report concludes.

options.text: Accept it, since the consultancy is a third party and therefore independent
options.why: Being a different legal entity is not independence. The test is whether they benefit from a particular result.

options.text: Accept it if the findings are detailed and include negative observations
options.why: A compromised assessor can include minor findings to appear credible. The conflict invalidates the process, not merely the tone.

options.text: Request evidence of the vendor's internal audits instead
options.why: Weaker still: that is the vendor grading its own work, which is why it is listed separately from independent assessment.

stem: Rank these three sources of vendor assurance from weakest to strongest in terms of objectivity.

options.text: Self-completed questionnaire, then evidence of the vendor's internal audits, then an independent third-party assessment
options.why: A questionnaire is what the vendor says. Internal audit is what the vendor's own assurance function found, which is better but still theirs. An independent assessment has no stake in the answer.

options.text: Independent assessment, then internal audit evidence, then questionnaire
options.why: Reversed. Independence makes an assessment stronger, not weaker.

options.text: Internal audit evidence, then questionnaire, then independent assessment
options.why: Internal audit is more objective than a self-completed questionnaire, not less.

options.text: They are equivalent, since all three come from the vendor
options.why: An independent assessment does not come from the vendor, which is the whole distinction.

stem: A customer wishes to penetration test a SaaS provider's platform. What must be established before any testing begins?

options.text: Contractual permission and written rules of engagement defining scope, timing, methods and contacts
options.why: Testing infrastructure you do not own without authorisation is unlawful, and on shared platforms it can affect other tenants. The rules of engagement bound all of that.

options.text: Nothing, provided the customer owns the data stored on the platform
options.why: Owning the data does not authorise testing someone else's systems, and on multi-tenant infrastructure the blast radius reaches other customers.

options.text: Only a non-disclosure agreement covering the findings
options.why: An NDA governs confidentiality of what is learned. It grants no permission to test.

options.text: A service level agreement specifying acceptable downtime during the test
options.why: An SLA sets performance commitments and is not an authorisation to test.

stem: Two firms intend to collaborate on a joint product. They need to define how they will share responsibility, revenue and liability in that partnership. Which agreement type covers this?

options.text: A business partners agreement
options.why: A BPA governs the terms of a partnership itself: contributions, responsibilities, revenue and liability between the parties.

options.text: A non-disclosure agreement
options.why: An NDA protects confidential information exchanged. It is almost always signed first and governs secrecy, not the commercial relationship.

options.text: A master service agreement
options.why: An MSA sets standing terms between a customer and a supplier, with individual work defined in statements of work beneath it. This is a partnership, not a supply arrangement.

options.text: A memorandum of understanding
options.why: An MOU records intent and is typically non-binding, which is the opposite of what liability allocation requires.

stem: An organisation has an MSA with a consultancy. It now wants a specific six-week engagement with defined deliverables and a price. Which document captures that?

options.text: A statement of work or work order under the existing MSA
options.why: The MSA holds the standing terms so they are not renegotiated each time; the SOW defines the specific scope, deliverables, timeline and price for one engagement.

options.text: A new master service agreement
options.why: The MSA already exists. Creating one per engagement defeats its purpose.

options.text: A memorandum of agreement
options.why: An MOA records agreed terms between parties, often where no commercial supply relationship exists. Here there is an MSA already.

options.text: A non-disclosure agreement
options.why: Governs confidentiality and defines no deliverables.

stem: A manufacturer assesses its direct suppliers carefully but has no visibility of who supplies them. A component compromise originates two tiers down. What was missing?

options.text: Supply chain analysis extending beyond tier one, since risk arrives through suppliers you did not contract with
options.why: Your exposure follows the chain, not your contracts. Assessing only direct suppliers leaves everything beneath them invisible, which is how component and dependency compromises land.

options.text: A right-to-audit clause with the direct suppliers
options.why: Useful and bounded by the contract. It gives no visibility of parties you have no agreement with.

options.text: More frequent questionnaires to direct suppliers
options.why: More of the same tier-one view, and self-reported at that.

options.text: A non-disclosure agreement covering component specifications
options.why: Protects confidentiality and has no bearing on upstream compromise.

stem: Which TWO statements about third-party risk management are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Due diligence informs the decision to engage; monitoring keeps the assessment current afterwards
options.why: They answer different questions at different points, which is why the objectives list both.

options.text: An assessor with a financial interest in the vendor cannot provide independent assurance
options.why: Conflict of interest invalidates the process regardless of what the report says.

options.text: A signed NDA demonstrates that a vendor's security controls are adequate
options.why: An NDA governs confidentiality of information shared. It asserts nothing about controls.

options.text: Evidence of a vendor's internal audits is equivalent to an independent assessment
options.why: Internal audit is the vendor's own function. Better than a questionnaire, not independent.

options.text: Assessing tier-one suppliers is sufficient, since they are responsible for their own suppliers
options.why: Responsibility can be passed down the chain; your exposure cannot.
